owner: options phase -- the `domain=` question. OPTIONS FOR THE OWNER, NOT A DECISION. Nothing in the repository was edited; every measurement below was taken on HEAD f31e35a with a clean worktree, from scratch scripts in /tmp/dom and the sweeps' own harnesses.
summary:
THE CHOICE YOU ARE ACTUALLY MAKING. Not "should levers have ranges" -- that question is already
answered YES by thirteen packages that wrote ranges by hand. The choice is WHERE THE UPPER END OF A
NUMBER LIVES, and whether "this lever has no ceiling" is a sentence somebody has to TYPE or a
sentence that is true by default because nobody typed anything. Every measurement below points at
that one seam. The tree's existing refusals are overwhelmingly LOWER bounds: of the ten OPT levers
with a startup refusal, seven are bounded below only, and those seven are exactly the ones the sweep
found harmful -- OPT_LR, OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY, OPT_GRAD_CLIP. The lower half of the problem is nearly
solved by hand already and is cheap to move into the declaration; the upper half is not solved
anywhere and is the half that produced FAB_ALPHA=1e26. So the options differ far less in their
lower bounds than in what they do about ceilings, and I have counted, per option, exactly how many
of the sweep's 37 findings each closes.

WHAT I RAN (tree at HEAD f31e35a, worktree clean at the time of every measurement below; a fixer
began editing src/fabric/api.py afterwards and that is noted where it matters). Nothing in the
repository was edited. Scratch at /tmp/dom/. Suite green before and after.
  * Reproduced the headline evidence on the LIVE tree through the fabric sweep's own harness
    (/tmp/fabsweep/cell.py, unmodified, fresh subprocess per cell):

        FAB_ALPHA=1e20     aux=0.5155787467956543  composed=2.7893991470336914  nonfinite 0/23
        FAB_ALPHA=1e24     aux=0.5156660079956055  composed=2.765979766845703   nonfinite 0/23
        FAB_ALPHA=1e26     aux=0.5150710344314575  composed=2.943258285522461   nonfinite 15/23

        FAB_ALPHA=nan      aux=nan                 composed=nan                 nonfinite 19/23
    and through the opt sweep's own harness (/tmp/sw/cell.py, unmodified):

        OPT_LR=1.0    five stages OK  p_finite=True   p_sample=[0.7911476492881775, ...]
        OPT_LR=100.0  five stages OK  p_finite=True   p_sample=[-0.07620048522949219, ...]

        OPT_LR=1e30   five stages OK  p_finite=FALSE  p_sample=[nan, nan, nan]
    NOTE THE NEW NUMBER IN THAT COLUMN AND IT MATTERS FOR EVERY OPTION: the model is DESTROYED at
    OPT_LR=1e6 (parameters at -3928) and still perfectly FINITE. The finiteness boundary and the
    harm boundary are twenty-four orders of magnitude apart. No ceiling that is chosen to stop nan
    is a ceiling that stops harm, and no ceiling that stops harm is derivable from the declaration.
  * Read src/spine/lever.py in full, .rework/audits/ruling_nonfinite.json, all six sweep_*.json
    with every legitimate_specials block, tests/test_census.py, docs/04_CONTRACT.md, DECISIONS D4,
    D11, D17, src/spine/units.py, and the range refusals in opt/lm/sig/cap/fab/data/world.
  * Enumerated and classified all 207 numeric levers by hand (/tmp/dom/classify.py, exact cover
    asserted against the live registry).

FOUR MEASURED FACTS THAT REFRAME THE QUESTION, AND YOU SHOULD SEE THEM BEFORE THE OPTIONS.

 1. THE UNIT LABEL IS NOT A DOMAIN, AND THIS TREE HAS ALREADY RULED THAT WAY THREE TIMES.
    75 of the 207 numeric levers carry U.FRACTION and 5 carry U.PROBABILITY -- 80 that LOOK as
    though the declaration already states a domain. It does not. src/fabric/api.py::build says so
    in its own words ("WHAT IS NOT REFUSED, AND WHY THE RULE IS NOT 'FRACTION MEANS 0..1'.
    U.FRACTION is a LABEL the census renders and not a bound"); src/tok/levers.py::TOKLevers says
    "a reader who takes 'fraction 0..1' as a bound on legal values will be surprised by 2.0, which
    is legal"; src/capacity/api.py::new_valve leaves CAP_LIFT > 1 legal on exactly that ground and
    adds "Refusing it would be this file deciding a range question the tree has twice decided the
    other way". SIG's own module header keeps two labels it calls wrong in principle. So the 80 are
    not 80 free domains; they are 80 places where writing (0.0, 1.0) would overturn three standing
    rulings at once. OPT_GRAD_CLIP is declared U.FRACTION and is a gradient-NORM threshold where 5.0
    is an ordinary setting; EVAL_GEN_TEMP and SIG_TEMP are declared U.FRACTION and are temperatures.

 2. AN OPEN UPPER END LETS +inf THROUGH. MEASURED, because the whole comparison turns on it
    (/tmp/dom/probe_shape.py):
        domain=(0.0, 1.0):   nan=REFUSED  inf=REFUSED  -inf=REFUSED  0=pass  0.5=pass  1e26=REFUSED
        domain=(0.0, None):  nan=REFUSED  inf=PASS     -inf=REFUSED  0=pass  0.5=pass  1e26=PASS
        domain=(None, 1.0):  nan=REFUSED  inf=REFUSED  -inf=pass     0=pass  0.5=pass  1e26=REFUSED
        domain=(1, None):    nan=REFUSED  inf=PASS     -inf=REFUSED  0=REFUSED  0.5=REFUSED  1e26=PASS
    ANY finite endpoint refuses nan for free. A finite LOW end refuses -inf. Only a finite HIGH end
    refuses +inf and 1e26. Under an honest, evidence-led population of `domain=`, 163 of the 207
    levers get no ceiling -- 53 of them floats -- so `domain=` ALONE leaves +inf legal on 53 float
    levers. That is why (2) and (3) are complements and not alternatives, and it is the strongest
    single argument in this report.

 3. THE OverflowError TOKEN HAS ALREADY LANDED, so option (2)'s scope is smaller than the prior
    ruling priced it. Measured on the live tree (/tmp/dom/probe_int.py):
        int lever  'inf' -> LeverError: YY_N='inf' is not a int        (was a bare OverflowError)
        int lever  'nan' -> LeverError   '-inf' -> LeverError   '1e999' -> LeverError
        float lever 'inf' -> inf    'nan' -> nan    '1e999' -> inf    '1e26' -> 1e+26
    All 110 int levers already refuse every non-finite spelling. A finiteness floor therefore
    governs the 97 FLOAT levers and nothing else -- and every one of the sweep's 24 non-finite
    findings is on a float lever. Two live holes remain at that same line, both measured:
        int lever '0.4'  -> 0        (silent truncation INTO a declared sentinel -- finding #1)
        int lever '1e26' -> 100000000000000004764729344   (a 27-digit width, accepted)

 4. `choices=` GENERALISES, AND IT HAS NEVER BEEN RUN ON A NUMBER. All 19 levers carrying
    `choices=` are str levers; ZERO of the 207 numeric levers carry one. I drove it on a numeric
    lever for the first time (/tmp/dom/probe_shape.py) and it behaves exactly as `domain=` would
    need to: declaration-time check against the default, post-coercion check in Lever.coerce,
    LeverError naming the generated env name and the value --
        ZZ_G='0.5' -> 0.5    ZZ_G='7' -> LeverError: ZZ_G=7.0 must be one of [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]
        ZZ_G='nan' -> LeverError    ZZ_G='inf' -> LeverError    ZZ_G='-inf' -> LeverError
    So the machinery cost of `domain=` really is small. The cost is elsewhere and it is prose and
    judgement, priced below.

=====================================================================================
WHAT I WOULD CHOOSE, AND THE EVIDENCE THAT WOULD MOVE ME
=====================================================================================
I WOULD TAKE (2) NOW AND (3) SLOWLY, WHICH IS THE PRIOR RULING'S R1+R2 -- but for a sharper reason
than that ruling gave, and with two amendments it did not make.
  * The sharper reason is fact 2 above: `domain=` populated honestly leaves +inf legal on 53 float
    levers, because 163 of 207 get no ceiling. (3) without (2) is not a smaller version of (2)+(3);
    it is a version that does not close the class the run was convened over on most of the surface.
  * AMENDMENT ONE: add the integrality clause to Lever.coerce in the same edit as the finiteness
    floor. `int(float(raw))` truncating 0.4 into a DECLARED DISARM (measured, finding #1) is not
    closed by (2), by (3), or by any of the four fixers' work, and it is one clause at the same line.
  * AMENDMENT TWO: write the domain as three fields and not a pair -- `domain=(lo, hi)` plus
    inclusivity -- or the shape cannot express what the tree already needs. Measured in ONE function
    (src/opt/api.py::build): `lr <= 0.0` is an OPEN low end, `min_frac` is [0.0, 1.0) HALF-OPEN, and
    `decay` is [0.0, 1.0] CLOSED. Three inclusivities in eleven clauses. src/lm/api.py::resolve
    needs the half-open one too (`0.0 <= dropout < 1.0`). A bare pair silently rounds all three to
    one and would either admit lr=0 or refuse decay=1.0.
I would NOT populate `domain=` beyond the 33 obvious ones without a measurement, and I would not
write a ceiling on FAB_ALPHA or OPT_LR from taste. src/fabric/api.py::build already names that
hazard by hand -- "a guard invented for a value nobody has shown to be wrong is the untrippable-
guard class one level up" -- and I confirmed it bites: FAB_HALT_MAX=1.5 is BIT-IDENTICAL to the
shipped default at the sweep's widths (aux 0.5120277404785156, composed 3.0068857669830322,
0/23 non-finite), so even the "obvious" ceiling of 1.0 on a probability refuses a value this tree
has not shown to be wrong at two passes.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, AND IT IS ONE AFTERNOON. Re-drive the 53 float levers whose
ceiling is not derivable at {1e12, 1e20, 1e26, 1e30} through the harnesses still on disk
(/tmp/fabsweep/, /tmp/sw/, /tmp/sigtok_sweep_5862/) -- ~212 cells, fresh subprocess each.
  IF the harm boundary clusters (say every one of them poisons somewhere in 1e20..1e30), then a
  SINGLE universal magnitude ceiling is defensible and option (2b) closes 25 of 37 for one constant,
  and (3) shrinks to the 33 obvious ones plus the eleven zeros. The headroom is measured and it is
  wide: the largest default in the tree is DATA_VAL_CAP=4000000, and the largest value this project
  has ever configured is CORPUS_CAP=100000000000 (1e11, in equiv.sh, bench_gpu.sh and longrun.sh),
  against a first measured harm at 1e26 -- fifteen orders of magnitude of room.
  IF instead each lever's boundary sits somewhere different -- which is what fp32 overflow at
  different widths and dtypes predicts, and FAB_ALPHA's boundary between 1e24 and 1e26 is one data
  point for it -- then NO universal ceiling exists, (2b) dies, and the honest answer is that the
  upper end is a per-lever measurement that arrives one lever at a time and `domain=` is the place
  to record it as it arrives.
THAT IS THE FALSIFIER FOR MY OWN RECOMMENDATION and I could not run it inside this phase's budget.

=====================================================================================
THE THINGS EVERY OPTION HAD TO ACCOUNT FOR
=====================================================================================
THE THREE GEOMETRY ZEROS -- and here I must contradict the brief, because I ran it. The brief says
FAB_RANK=0, FAB_DK=0 and SIG_D=0 are "in-range for any plausible domain" and that "NO (lo,hi) RULE
CATCHES THEM". Measured on the live tree at f31e35a through the fabric sweep's own harness:
    FAB_RANK=0  aux=nan  A_shape=[12,16,0]      FAB_RANK=1  aux=0.5270954370498657  clean
    FAB_DK=0    aux=nan                          FAB_DK=1    aux=0.5049235224723816  clean
`domain=(1, None)` on a width DOES catch all three -- a finite low end refuses 0 (proved in fact 2
above) -- and the neighbouring legal value builds clean, so it over-refuses nothing. None of the
three has a declared 0-meaning anywhere and all three are ACCEPTED_HARMFUL in the sweeps, not
ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE. WHAT IS TRUE, and is the brief's point standing on firmer ground: a pair
catches the ZERO and not the CLASS. The class is "a geometry that produces a well-formed meaningless
number", and its other members are RELATIONAL -- LM_WIDTH % LM_HEADS, WORLD_N0 <= WORLD_NMAX,
DATA_SEG_MIN <= DATA_SEG_MAX, MEM_KEY_DEPTH <= LM_LAYERS, LM_CTX <= d_pos_max -- 15 of the 207 by my
count, and not one of them is expressible as a per-lever pair. Those belong at the read site
forever, which is why option (5) does not go away under any of the others.

ZERO IS A LOADED VALUE. 46 of the 207 have a low value whose meaning is declared or measured
legitimate, and the declarations are in three different places: 22 in the help string (which
docs/04_LEVERS.md would render), the rest only in a declaration comment or in the api body
(MEM_REKEY_EVERY's DISARM is in memory/api.py::maintain, MEM_PROBE_EVERY's in the declaration
comment, DOM_CULL_FRAC's only as a counter name `n_cull_budget_zero`). An author writing `domain=`
from the declaration alone will get 24 of those 46 wrong. That is a per-lever review cost, not a
per-lever typing cost, and it is the honest number for "what (3) really costs".

THE OPT CASE, AND WHAT IT IMPLIES FOR (5) SPECIFICALLY. Eleven refusals over ten levers, all passing
1e30 -- verified. But the interesting structure is not that they missed a value; it is WHICH HALF
they wrote. Three of the ten levers are bounded at BOTH ends (damp, min_frac, decay) and seven are
bounded BELOW ONLY (lr, weight_decay, grad_clip, warmup, wavelength, accum, batch_windows). The
three two-sided ones are all shares of something, where the ceiling is obvious. The seven one-sided
ones are all magnitudes, where it is not. So (5)'s failure is not carelessness and it is not
placement: a careful author at the read site, holding the mechanism, writes the bound whose
violation they can PICTURE (a negative rate) and omits the one they cannot (a rate 24 orders of
magnitude too large). Moving the check to the declaration does not fix that BY ITSELF -- `hi=None`
is one keystroke -- which is why the only version of (3) that actually addresses the OPT case is the
one where the upper end must be TYPED (see option 3b in the findings). That version costs a
207-declaration migration and forecloses the incremental path. It is a genuine trade and I have not
resolved it for you.

D17. It does not reach here on its own terms and the tree has already said so: src/ckpt/api.py's
REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD block states "It is NOT a precedent that a range refusal gets a switch...
This switch exists because the owner asked for THIS refusal to be turn-off-able, by name". If you
nonetheless want the D17 shape, note what docs/04_CONTRACT.md already records about the one that
shipped: flipping REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD costs "a code edit in five files", and the document itself
concludes that the answer to "is the refusal turn-off-able without editing code" is NO. A parse-time
rule can do better on the spelling (ONE constant in spine/lever.py, reachable by everyone, because
O10's allowlist already contains spine.lever) and CANNOT do better on the substance: an environment
switch would have to be a raw os.environ read inside Lever.coerce -- legal, since lever.py is the one
file O1 permits to name the environment, but it would be the tree's first environment name that is
not a lever, invisible to the registry, to the census and to docs/04_LEVERS.md. That is precisely
the shape lever.py's own module header exists to end ("tokenizer.py read TOK_MINT_PMIN straight from
os.environ, invisible to the registry and to every audit built on it"). ONE SWITCH, NOT MANY, and if
you want it reachable from a shell you are accepting that one knob back. I would take the constant.

WIRE_BUDGET. Verified rather than assumed: WIRE_BUDGET=25, COUPLINGS declares 23 rows, and a real
build spends 19 -- six edges remain. NONE of options (1)-(5) spends one. A domain is an attribute of
a declaration the owning package already holds; the check runs inside spine.lever, which every
package imports by O10's allowlist. The only shape in this report that would need a wire is a
RELATIONAL domain (LM_CTX <= d_pos_max is already a wire and already checked at the read site), and
I am not proposing one.

findings.lever: OPTION (1) -- NOTHING CENTRAL: fix each defect where it lives
findings.detail: CLOSES BY RULE: 0 of 37. Closes 35 by hand -- which is what the four fixers are doing today and it is real work that should land regardless. The two it CANNOT close are the two that are properties of Lever.coerce and have no package to live in: #0 (large finite magnitudes) and #1 (a fractional string truncating into a declared sentinel). PRICE WHEN LEVER 208 IS ADDED, which is the question that decides this option. Today a new lever is one line in a levers.py, and NOTHING in the suite asks whether its range was ever considered. I checked: tests/test_census.py joins on lever NAMES and reads no other Lever field (the only occurrence of `Lever(` in that file is inside a comment); tests/test_contract.py::declared_levers parses `Lever(...)` by AST and records only the assignment TARGET, so it is blind to every kwarg; and no check anywhere enumerates which levers have a bound. So a reader asking 'was a domain checked on this lever' has one way to find out: grep the owning api.py for the field name and read what comes back. THAT IS THE ANSWER TO 'how would a reader know a domain was ever checked' -- they would not, and that is true today. THE RECORD IS NOT NEUTRAL ON THIS OPTION. The best per-package refusal in the tree, src/fabric/api.py::build, wrote out by hand the eight levers it was DECLINING to cover (FAB_ALPHA, FAB_ROUTE_T, FAB_HALT_MAX, FAB_BAL_FLOOR, FAB_SPAWN_FLOOR, FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W, FAB_MUT, FAB_PRESSURE) and five of those eight carry a critical finding today. The defect did not close, it RELOCATED into the list its own author wrote. WHAT THIS OPTION IS RIGHT ABOUT, and no other option supplies it: 15 of the 207 have a ceiling that is ANOTHER LEVER, and a per-lever declaration cannot express any of them.

findings.lever: OPTION (2) -- A FINITENESS FLOOR ONLY, in Lever.coerce, behind one switch
findings.detail: CLOSES BY RULE: 23 of 37 outright, plus the +inf half of #16 (OPT_LR), so 24 findings are touched and 13 are missed. COUNTED, NOT ESTIMATED, from ruling_nonfinite.json by the value each repro drives: 24 findings are triggered by nan/+inf/-inf (#2,3,4,5,6,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,19,20,21,22,23,26,27,30,31,32,33,34); 11 by ZERO (#7,8,9,10,18,24,25,28,29,35,36); 1 by a large finite value (#0); 1 by a non-integral string (#1). 24+11+1+1 = 37. ITS SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN THE PRIOR RULING PRICED IT, and this is new: the OverflowError token has ALREADY LANDED at src/spine/lever.py:134, so all 110 int levers already refuse 'inf', '-inf', 'nan' and '1e999' with the tree's own LeverError. A finiteness floor governs the 97 FLOAT levers and nothing else. Every one of the 24 non-finite findings is on a float lever, so the count is unaffected -- but 'ten lines that change the meaning of 207 declarations' is now 'ten lines that change the meaning of 97'. That halves the blast radius the prior ruling asked for a switch about. THE 1e26 MEASUREMENT IS THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT AND IT IS DECISIVE ON ITS OWN TERMS: FAB_ALPHA =1e26 leaves the loss reading 0.515 / 2.94 with 15 of 23 gradients already non-finite, and OPT_LR=1e6 -- fourteen orders of magnitude BELOW any finiteness boundary -- drives every parameter to -3928 with all five stages reporting OK. A finiteness rule closes a spelling. WHAT IT IS STILL WORTH, and I would still land it: it is the only option that covers a body that DOES NOT EXIST YET. Roughly 288 cells across the six sweeps are UNREACHABLE_TODAY because the consumer is a P4/P5/P6 stub -- 33 FAB levers, all 23 DOM+MEM floats, 14 of EVAL's 15 -- and one of them already crosses a package boundary (FAB_COMP_EMA=nan -> DOM.d_comp_ema=nan, no warning). Every per-package refusal must be written by the author who writes the body; a parse-layer rule is written once, now.

findings.lever: OPTION (2b) -- (2) PLUS ONE UNIVERSAL MAGNITUDE CEILING  [not in the brief; the evidence suggests it]
findings.detail: CLOSES BY RULE: 24 outright plus #0, so 25 of 37, missing 12. It is the only option in this report that reaches the finding that made the question urgent WITHOUT asking anyone to defend a per-lever ceiling. THE SHAPE: one constant in spine/lever.py, e.g. |v| <= 1e15 for every numeric lever, refused at the same line as the finiteness clause and in the same idiom, with a per-Lever opt-out. It asserts nothing about any lever's mechanism -- it asserts that no lever in THIS project is a number that large. THE HEADROOM IS MEASURED AND IT IS WIDE. Largest default in the whole tree: DATA_VAL_CAP = 4000000. Largest value this project has ever CONFIGURED, found by grepping every script: CORPUS_CAP=100000000000 (1e11) in equiv.sh:65, bench_gpu.sh:94 and longrun.sh:579 -- the 40GB corpus arm. First measured harm: FAB_ALPHA between 1e24 (clean, 0/23) and 1e26 (15/23). So a ceiling anywhere in 1e12..1e20 sits above every configuration this project has ever run and below every harm it has ever measured. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, said plainly so it is not oversold: it does not touch OPT_LR=1e6, which destroys the model and is finite and small. It buys the top of the range and nothing else. WHY IT IS HONEST WHERE A PER-LEVER CEILING FROM TASTE IS NOT: it makes exactly one claim, the claim is checkable against every configuration in the repository, and it does not pretend to know any mechanism. THE HAZARD, named: int levers. `1e26` on an int lever today coerces to the 27-digit integer 100000000000000004764729344 (measured), which a width lever would then try to allocate. A universal ceiling closes that too -- which is a second finding it picks up for free, and one no sweep has filed.

findings.lever: OPTION (3) -- domain=(lo, hi) PER LEVER, populated incrementally  [the main option]
findings.detail: CLOSES BY RULE, populated conservatively (only where a bound is obvious from the declaration): 22 of 37 outright plus 2 half -- 9 of the 11 zeros (#7 FAB_RANK, #8 FAB_DK, #9 MEM_QUOTA, #10 FAB_EMB_HID, #18 SIG_D, #24 SIG_CONTRASTIVE_BATCH, #25 TOK_MAX_BYTES, #29 MEM_OWNERS, #36 FAB_HOPS), half of #28 (FAB_MANAGE_EVERY also needs spine/derive.py), NOT #35 (FAB_SLOTS=0 is legitimate at FAB.build), and 13 of the 24 non-finite ones as a side effect of any finite endpoint refusing nan (#3 partly, #4, #5, #6, #12, #13, #19, #20, #21, #27, #30, #31, #33). IT MISSES 11 OF THE 24 NON-FINITE FINDINGS, and this is the fact the proposal turns on: #2 FAB_ALPHA=nan, #11 FAB_BAL_FLOOR=-inf, #14 SIG_VAR_WEIGHT=inf, #15 SIG_COV_WEIGHT=inf, #16 OPT_LR=inf, #17 OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=inf, #22 SIG_TEMP=inf, #23 SIG_WARMUP_PLATEAU_EPS=inf, #26 FAB_ROUTE_T=inf, #32 OPT_GRAD_CLIP=inf, #34 DATA_EXPOSURE=inf -- every one of them a lever whose ceiling is not derivable, so it gets hi=None, and hi=None ADMITS +inf (measured). THE HONEST PRICE, MEASURED. Of the 207: the LOW end is obvious on 149, is a declared or measured sentinel on 46 (which you learn from the api body, not the declaration -- only 22 of the 207 mention their special value in the help string at all), needs a judgement on 5, is NEGATIVE on 2 (EVAL_GENUINE_SIL is a silhouette in [-1,1]; MEM_MATCH_FLOOR is a cosine similarity -- a reflexive lo=0.0 is simply wrong on both), depends on another lever's ARM on 2, is CONTESTED BETWEEN TWO READERS on 1 (MEM_REKEY_EVERY), is deliberately undecided on 1 (EVAL_CURVE_EVERY), and does not exist on 1 (RUN_SEED). The HIGH end is obvious on 44, is a policy the tree has explicitly declined three times on 16, is another lever on 15, and IS NOT DERIVABLE AT ALL ON 131. BOTH ENDS OBVIOUS: 33 of 207 -- DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC, DOM_CULL_FRAC, DOM_DECAY, DOM_MERGE_DIST, DOM_PRIOR_BLEND, DOM_RADIUS_Q, DOM_SHIFT_DIST, DOM_SHIFT_Q, DOM_SPAWN_DIST, DOM_TOKC_DECAY, EVAL_AFF_MIN, FAB_CULL_FRAC, FAB_DISCOVER, FAB_HALT_MAX, FAB_LR_AMIN, FAB_LR_GAMMA, FAB_MERGE_DIST, FAB_MUT_BIG_P, FAB_NEW_FRAC, FAB_PARENT_MAX, FAB_PRESSURE, FAB_XOVER, LM_DROPOUT, MEM_PRESSURE_THRESH, MEM_PROBATION_FRAC, MEM_USE_DECAY, MEM_WRITE_GATE, MEM_WRITE_TARGET, OPT_LR_DECAY, OPT_LR_MIN_FRAC, OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP, SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC, TOK_DROPOUT. NOT ONE OF THE SEVEN LEVERS THE SWEEP FILED AS CRITICAL FOR A MAGNITUDE IS IN THAT LIST. THE MACHINERY COST IS GENUINELY SMALL and I drove it rather than assuming: `choices=` is an optional kwarg, validated at declaration time against the default, checked in coerce after coercion, raising LeverError with the generated env name -- and driven on a NUMERIC lever for the first time (all 19 of its users today are str levers; ZERO numeric levers carry one) it refuses 7, nan, inf and -inf correctly. LeverView would take one field and has one producer (spine/lever.py::Config.lever) and no consumer in src/, tests/ or tools/. No census row, no env name, no wire. THE COST THAT IS NOT SMALL IS PROSE, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE PRIOR RULING SAID. It counted ten citations in seven files; I count THIRTEEN sites in EIGHT files asserting as a load-bearing premise that a Lever has no range facility: src/sig/levers.py:511, src/sig/api.py:806, src/lm/api.py:205, src/lm/api.py:235, src/train/levers.py:187, src/opt/levers.py:274, src/opt/api.py:688, src/capacity/levers.py:436, src/capacity/api.py:661, src/capacity/api.py:677, src/spine/derive.py:334, src/spine/derive.py:370, src/spine/derive.py:672. O13 will not catch any of them: it checks that a cited path::symbol exists, not that a sentence about it is still true. THE SHAPE MUST BE THREE FIELDS, NOT A PAIR, and this is measured in one function: src/opt/api.py::build needs an OPEN low end (`lr <= 0.0`), a HALF-OPEN interval (`not 0.0 <= min_frac < 1.0`) and a CLOSED one (`not 0.0 <= decay <= 1.0`) -- three inclusivities in eleven clauses -- and src/lm/api.py::resolve needs the half-open one again for LM_DROPOUT. findings.lever: OPTION (3b) -- domain= WITH A MANDATORY EXPLICIT UPPER END  [not in the brief; the OPT case suggests it]
findings.detail: THE VARIANT THAT ACTUALLY ADDRESSES THE OPT CASE, and the only one that does. Same kwarg, one rule added: the field is REQUIRED on every Lever, and 'no ceiling' must be written -- domain=(0.0, UNBOUNDED) -- rather than omitted. WHY THE EVIDENCE POINTS AT IT. The OPT failure is not that eleven refusals were placed in the wrong file. It is which HALF each author wrote. Of the ten OPT levers carrying a startup refusal, THREE are bounded at both ends (lr_restart_damp, lr_min_frac, lr_decay -- all three are shares, where the ceiling is obvious) and SEVEN are bounded below only (lr, weight_decay, grad_clip, lr_warmup, lr_wavelength, accum, batch_windows -- all magnitudes or counts, where it is not). The same shape in LM: six of seven per-lever refusals are lower-only, and the one two-sided refusal is LM_DROPOUT, a probability. Authors write the bound whose violation they can picture. Under plain option (3), `hi=None` is one keystroke and reproduces the omission exactly, in a new place. WHAT IT COSTS AND WHAT IT FORECLOSES, which is why it is an option and not a recommendation: it is a 207-declaration migration in one commit, it forecloses the incremental path R2 was designed around, and 131 of those 207 declarations would carry UNBOUNDED -- which is either the most valuable line in the file (a written, reviewable claim that nobody has bounded this) or 131 lines of ceremony, and I cannot tell you which from here. A CHEAPER HALF-MEASURE THAT KEEPS MOST OF THE VALUE: make the field optional, but have the declaration-time check REFUSE a domain with an open upper end on a FLOAT lever unless the declaration also carries an explicit `unbounded_above=True`. That confines the ceremony to the 97 floats, which is where +inf and 1e26 actually live.

findings.lever: OPTION (4) -- A DOMAIN EXPRESSED AS A TYPE (Probability, PositiveInt, Fraction, Bytes)
findings.detail: CLOSES THE SAME 22+2 AS (3): it is a different spelling of the same check, so it inherits (3)'s catch profile exactly and differs only in cost and in what it invites. IS IT THE SAME IDEA AS units.py's CLOCK KINDS WEARING THE SAME CLOTHES? NO, AND units.py SAYS SO ITSELF, IN ITS OWN OPENING. That file draws exactly this line and gives the reason: '1. UNIT AS METADATA, for every lever and every reported number. Cheap, always correct, never enforced. 2. UNIT AS A RUNTIME TYPE, for CLOCKS ONLY. This is where the bugs actually were, every time.' The Clock kinds are a runtime type because a clock is 'one number compared against one threshold -- that is a small enough surface to type honestly'. A Probability is not that shape: it is not compared against another Probability, it is multiplied into a tensor. Steps(4000) >= Flushes(250) raising is a statement about a COMPARISON between two values; Probability(1.5) refusing is a statement about ONE value's range. Those are different mechanisms and units.py's header is a ruling against conflating them ('a proposal to catch the whole family with a static checker was rejected during design review'). WHAT THE TYPE FORM BUYS OVER THE PAIR, and it is real: a name is reusable and a pair is not, so 'this is a Probability' is reviewable in a way '(0.0, 1.0)' is not, and the 33 both-ends-obvious levers collapse into about five names -- Probability (4), Share/Fraction of a finite set (~20), Quantile (3), CosineDistance (5, ceiling 2.0 not 1.0), Similarity/Silhouette (2, floor -1.0). WHAT IT COSTS OVER THE PAIR: a second vocabulary in the spine that must be kept in step with units.py's fourteen unit constants, which today are LABELS -- and the tree has three standing rulings that the label is not a bound (fabric/api.py::build, tok/levers.py::TOKLevers, capacity/api.py::new_valve). Introducing a Probability TYPE beside a PROBABILITY LABEL, where the type binds and the label does not, is two things with one name. If you take (4), the honest version REPLACES the relevant unit constants rather than sitting beside them -- and that is a spine edit touching every declaration, i.e. (3b)'s migration with extra steps. THE CASE WHERE THE TYPE IS STRICTLY BETTER: EVAL_GENUINE_SIL and MEM_MATCH_FLOOR both have a lower bound of -1.0, and a pair written from habit gets both wrong. A type named Similarity cannot be got wrong.
findings.repro: cd /home/user/LLM-Test && sed -n '1,25p' src/spine/units.py -- the two-strengths split, quoted above. sed -n '366,382p' src/spine/units.py -- the fourteen label constants and CLOCK_KINDS. The three label-is-not-a-bound rulings: src/fabric/api.py:437-441, src/tok/levers.py:487-489, src/capacity/api.py:659-670.

findings.lever: OPTION (5) -- VALIDATE AT THE READ SITE, each package refusing in its own build()
findings.detail: CLOSES BY RULE: 0 of 37 -- it is what the tree already does, and the 37 are what it produced. But it must not be dismissed, because it is the ONLY option that reaches two whole classes, and the brief is right that the read site knows the mechanism. WHAT IT BUYS THAT NO CENTRAL RULE CAN, counted: (a) THE RELATIONAL BOUNDS -- 15 of the 207 have a ceiling that is another lever or a wire, and not one is expressible per-lever: LM_WIDTH % LM_HEADS != 0 on the transformer arm (which src/lm/api.py::resolve calls 'the LOCAL coupling over (LM.width, LM.heads) that belongs to something holding both'), WORLD_N0 > WORLD_NMAX, DATA_SEG_MIN > DATA_SEG_MAX, MEM_KEY_DEPTH <= LM_LAYERS, LM_CTX <= d_pos_max. (b) THE ARM-DEPENDENT ONES -- DATA_N_PROCESSES=0 is refused by name on DATA_SOURCE=synthetic and correctly inert on real; SIG_MODE=bigram refuses width<2 while learned refuses width<1. A per-lever pair cannot say 'illegal on one arm'. (c) THE SENTINEL RESOLUTIONS -- LM_LAYERS=0 becoming 4 or 1 by arm, and being RECORDED as layers_from_sentinel so the report can say which number ran. WHAT THE OPT CASE IMPLIES FOR IT SPECIFICALLY, and it is not what it first looks like. Eleven refusals passing 1e30 is NOT evidence that read-site checks are worth little -- they are worth a great deal, and I would keep every one. It is evidence about WHICH HALF a careful author writes: seven of the ten OPT levers with a refusal are bounded BELOW ONLY, and the three that are bounded above are the three that are shares of something. The author of opt/api.py::build knew the mechanism perfectly and still did not write a ceiling on a learning rate, because the value that breaks it is 1e30 and nobody pictures 1e30. Mechanism knowledge supplies the LOWER bound reliably and the UPPER bound not at all, on this tree's record, in the file that knows the mechanism best. THE SECOND STRUCTURAL FACT, from the opt sweep and worth repeating because it is the sharpest sentence in the six reports: every guard that HELD against NaN has the inverted-chain form (`if not 0.0 <= x < 1.0`), and the levers that are safe today are safe BY GRAMMAR, NOT BY INTENT. 207 of these is thirteen authors each rediscovering that `x < 0` is False for NaN, at thirteen different times, some of them not yet. SO: (5) IS NOT AN ALTERNATIVE TO (2) OR (3). It is the residue that survives all of them, and the right question is not whether to keep it but whether moving the 33 obvious per-lever bounds out of bodies and into declarations makes the remaining read-site checks EASIER TO SEE -- I think it does, because what would be left in a body is exactly the relational and arm-dependent work that genuinely needs the body.

findings.lever: THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDES BETWEEN (2) AND (3): an open upper end admits +inf
findings.detail:
THIS IS THE ONE RESULT I WOULD NOT WANT THE OWNER TO DECIDE WITHOUT. The brief, and the prior ruling, both treat (2) as a floor and (3) as the answer. The arithmetic says something stronger and more specific: they cover DISJOINT halves of the special-value surface, and neither is a subset of the other. MEASURED (/tmp/dom/probe_shape.py):
    domain=(0.0, 1.0):   nan=REFUSED  inf=REFUSED  -inf=REFUSED  1e26=REFUSED
    domain=(0.0, None):  nan=REFUSED  inf=PASS     -inf=REFUSED  1e26=PASS
    domain=(None, 1.0):  nan=REFUSED  inf=REFUSED  -inf=pass     1e26=REFUSED
    domain=(1, None):    nan=REFUSED  inf=PASS     -inf=REFUSED  0=REFUSED
ANY finite endpoint refuses nan for free -- so `domain=` picks up 13 of the 24 non-finite findings at no extra cost, which is a real bonus nobody had counted. But +inf is refused ONLY by a finite upper end, and under an evidence-led population 163 of 207 levers get none -- 53 of them floats, which is where +inf can be coerced at all. So `domain=` alone leaves +inf legal on 53 float levers including OPT_LR, OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY, SIG_VAR_WEIGHT, SIG_COV_WEIGHT and FAB_ROUTE_T -- five of the sweep's own critical findings. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DECISION: if you take exactly one of (2) and (3), you are choosing which half of the surface to leave open, not choosing a weaker and a stronger rule. (2) alone leaves every zero and every large finite. (3) alone leaves +inf on 53 floats. Only together do they reach 33 of 37.

findings.lever: THE THREE GEOMETRY ZEROS -- the brief's claim, tested and refuted
findings.detail:
THE BRIEF SAYS: 'FAB_RANK=0, FAB_DK=0 and SIG_D=0 are finite, in-range for any plausible domain ... NO (lo,hi) RULE CATCHES THEM.' I ran it and that is not so. A finite LOW end refuses 0 -- domain=(1, None) on a width catches all three -- and the neighbouring legal value builds clean, so it over-refuses nothing. MEASURED on the live tree through the fabric sweep's own harness:
    FAB_RANK=0  -> aux=nan  A_shape=[12,16,0]   (rank-0 adapters, dW identically zero forever)
    FAB_RANK=1  -> aux=0.5270954370498657  composed=3.021953582763672  0/23 non-finite
    FAB_DK=0    -> aux=nan
    FAB_DK=1    -> aux=0.5049235224723816  composed=2.999781608581543  0/23 non-finite
None of the three has a declared 0-meaning anywhere -- I checked all 207 help strings, the declaration comments, and all six sweeps' ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE lists -- and all three are filed ACCEPTED_HARMFUL. So the bound is defensible from the declaration and costs nothing. WHAT IS TRUE, AND IS THE BRIEF'S POINT ON FIRMER GROUND: a pair catches the ZERO, not the CLASS. The class is 'a geometry that produces a well-formed meaningless number', and its other members are RELATIONAL: LM_WIDTH % LM_HEADS, WORLD_N0 <= WORLD_NMAX, DATA_SEG_MIN <= DATA_SEG_MAX, MEM_KEY_DEPTH <= LM_LAYERS, LM_CTX <= d_pos_max -- 15 of 207 by my count, none expressible as a per-lever pair, all of them permanently option (5)'s. SO THE ANSWER TO 'WHAT CATCHES THEM' IS: the zeros by a domain, the relations by a read-site refusal, and there is no single mechanism that does both. ONE MORE THING THE ZEROS SHOW, and it is the reason a domain is worth more than eleven hand refusals: nine of the eleven zero findings are WIDTHS AND COUNTS in FIVE different packages (FAB, MEM, SIG, TOK). Under option (1) that is nine refusals by five authors at five times.

findings.lever: ZERO IS A LOADED VALUE -- 46 of 207, and the declarations are in three different places
findings.detail: COUNTED OVER ALL 207 rather than the nine the brief cites from MEM and DOM. 46 numeric levers have a low value whose meaning is declared or was measured legitimate by a sweep. That is 22% of the surface, and it is the per-lever REVIEW cost of option (3) -- not the typing cost. THE HAZARD IS NOT THAT THEY EXIST, IT IS WHERE THEY ARE WRITTEN. Only 22 of the 207 mention their special value in the HELP STRING (the text docs/04_LEVERS.md would render): CAP_FAB_START, CAP_VOCAB_START, CKPT_EVERY, DATA_PHASE_LIVE, DOM_PRIOR_BLEND, DOM_RADIUS_CAP, DOM_TOKC_DECAY, FAB_DEPTH0, FAB_LR_GAMMA, FAB_ROUTE_REGION_W, LM_LAYERS, MEM_BLEND_MAX, MEM_JUDGE_FRAC, MEM_KEY_DEPTH, MEM_MATCH_FLOOR, OPT_GRAD_CLIP, OPT_LR, OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH, TOK_FREEZE_AT, TOK_MINT_NOVEL, TOK_MINT_PMIN, TOK_RETOK_EVERY. AN AUTHOR WRITING `domain=` FROM THE DECLARATION ALONE GETS 24 OF THE 46 WRONG. THE ONE THAT NO DOMAIN CAN GET RIGHT, and it must not be folded into this ruling: MEM_REKEY_EVERY=0 is the declared DISARM for memory/api.py::maintain AND, through rekey_period -> Windows(0) -> RUN.Cadences.due, means 'fire every window' for the other reader. AND THE OTHER DIRECTION: 75 of the six sweeps' 828 cells are ACCEPTED_LEGITIMATE and every single one is a zero -- not one is nan, +inf or -inf. No option in this report proposes one, and none should.

findings.lever: THE TWO SPINE-LEVEL FINDINGS NO OPTION IN THE BRIEF CLOSES
findings.detail: #1 NON-INTEGRAL TRUNCATION. `v = int(float(raw))` in Lever.coerce truncates toward zero with no warning, so a fractional value lands on 0 -- and 0 is a DECLARED SENTINEL on several of these levers, which means the operator asking for the tightest setting receives the OFF switch. STILL LIVE, measured on the current tree: an int lever at '0.4' resolves to 0. No finiteness rule catches it, no (lo, hi) pair catches it (0 is inside the domain on a cadence), and no per-package refusal can see it because by the time the package reads the Config the fraction is gone -- Config.given() still reports the string '0.4' beside a mechanism running at 0, which is the false-equation class with a sentinel as its subject. It is ONE CLAUSE at the same line as the finiteness check and it should ride along with whichever option is taken. AND A SECOND, WHICH NO SWEEP HAS FILED: an int lever at '1e26' resolves to the integer 100000000000000004764729344. On a width lever that is an allocation request; on a cadence it is a silent never. Only option (2b)'s universal ceiling reaches it. #0 LARGE FINITE MAGNITUDES is the other, and it is priced in the (2b) and (3) entries. The thing to hold on to is the shape of the gap: FAB_ALPHA is clean at 1e24 and 15/23 poisoned at 1e26 WITH THE LOSS STILL READING 0.515 / 2.94, and OPT_LR destroys every parameter at 1e6 while every number in the ledger stays finite. There is no single value of any lever at which 'the run went wrong' becomes visible in the report, which is the real reason this class is hard and the reason I would not claim any option here closes it.

findings.lever: D17, THE SWITCH, AND WHY AN ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLE SWITCH IS THE ONE SHAPE TO REFUSE
findings.detail: DOES D17 REACH HERE? NOT ON ITS OWN TERMS, AND THE TREE HAS ALREADY SAID SO IN THE FILE THAT IMPLEMENTS IT. src/ckpt/api.py's REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD block: 'It is NOT a precedent that a range refusal gets a switch, and the tree it lands in is emphatic about that: lm/api.py::resolve, opt/api.py::build and capacity/api.py::new_valve all refuse out-of-range lever values with no switch of any kind... This switch exists because the owner asked for THIS refusal to be turn-off-able, by name, in the same breath as ordering it -- and it is the only one in the tree that was asked for.' ONE SWITCH, NOT MANY, IF YOU WANT ONE. D17's shipped shape is spelled five times because O10 forbids four packages to import ckpt. A parse-time rule has no such problem: O10's allowlist already contains spine.lever, so ONE module constant in the file that owns parsing is reachable everywhere by construction. And a `domain=` needs no switch at all -- its blast radius is one lever and deleting the kwarg is the switch. So: a switch for a CENTRAL rule (option 2 or 2b), none for a per-lever declaration (option 3, 4). THE SHAPE TO REFUSE, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH THE OWNER'S ATTENTION. If D17's literal requirement is applied -- turn-off-able WITHOUT EDITING CODE -- then the switch must be an environment variable, and a parse-time rule cannot express one as a Lever: the lever system is the thing being guarded, and the switch must be read before any Config exists. It would have to be a raw os.environ read inside Lever.coerce. That is LEGAL -- src/spine/lever.py is the one file tests/test_ownership.py::check_o1_one_env_reader permits to name the environment -- and it would be the tree's first environment name that is not a lever: invisible to the registry, to tests/test_census.py (whose N1/N2 join on lever names), and to docs/04_LEVERS.md. That is precisely the failure lever.py's own module header exists to end: 'tokenizer.py read TOK_MINT_PMIN and TOK_MINT_GATE_K straight from os.environ, invisible to the registry and to every audit built on it.' I would take the module constant and record the D17 gap in docs/04_CONTRACT.md, exactly as that document already does for the five period refusals -- it states in its own words that the answer to 'is the refusal turn-off-able without editing code' is NO, and says so rather than paraphrasing the requirement down.
